main_text.p: minus venditabant se stare pro illibata Reipub. libertate adversus tyrannum; polteàà Deo percussos Historiographi, qui de ejus vita & morte aliquid literis tradiderant, diligenter observaverunt omnes. Profitetur {y}Appianus se duos integros Libros, tertium & quartum de civilibus Romanorum bellis, in ac-curata hujus eventus disquisitione im-pendere: {z}Plutarchus vero ipse quidem Græcus, sed in rebus Romanis verfatif-simus pariter & oculatissimus his ver-bis hanc Tragœdiam suo more genti-litio eleganter describit: Magnus ille suus, quo viuens usus erat Genius, e-jus quoque defuncti necis authores,ul-tor subsequutus est: omnes namque terras & maria peragrans eosque inve-stigavit, ut ex percussoribus neminem relinqueret, quin in stragem dederit u-niversos: cæterum, ex humanis quidem rebus id præcipuè admirationis extitit, quod Cassio evenit, eodem siquidem pugione, quo in Cæsarem usus fuerat, seipsum interemit: ex divinis autem, stella ingens crinita, quæ cum post Cæ-saris intetitum ad septem usque noctes eximio

page.notes: The marginal notes are set in small italic type. The first note is "In princip.lib.1.de bellis civil.", the second "In vita Caii Cæsaris". Their letters y and z correspond to the marks in the text. The word after "polteàà" is doubtful and may be "postea à"; marked as printed. The word "Cassio" is read from a long-s form. The last line "eximio" is set flush right and the paragraph continues on the next page. The number "13" is read as printed in the top right corner.
